items.prompt: Your draft commit message is 'fix(estimator): stop polling after the subscription delivers and rename the GanttChart props'. What does the guide tell you to do?
distractors: Keep it as one commit, but move the second half of the summary into the commit body
Keep it, because both changes touch the same estimator scope
Squash it into the next commit so the PR ends up with fewer commits overall
items.explanation: If you can't describe a commit in one sentence without 'and', it holds two ideas; a reviewer reading commit-by-commit should never hold two unrelated changes at once.

items.prompt: What belongs in a commit body, according to the repo's guide?
items.answer: The why the diff can't show: the reason, why now, any intended behaviour change
distractors: A file-by-file list of what changed, so reviewers can skip reading the diff
The story text
Nothing: the subject line should carry everything a reviewer needs to know
items.explanation: The applyProjectToState example names the bug the duplication caused, why the refactor is happening now (HN-01 needs a fifth caller), and the one intended behaviour change.

items.prompt: Where does the story id (HN-xx) go in this repo's workflow?
items.answer: In the branch name and the commit body, not the subject
distractors: Only in the commit subject, as a prefix like [HN-01]
Only in the PR title; branch names and commit messages stay deliberately generic
Nowhere: the pull request template links the story automatically from the branch
items.explanation: Putting the id in the branch makes branch, commits and PR searchable together; the subject stays a conventional-commit summary.

items.prompt: Why does this repo merge PRs with merge commits (--no-ff) rather than squash or rebase?
items.answer: So `git log --first-parent` reads as a list of shipped stories
distractors: Because squash merges lose the original author's identity on the commit
Amplify can't deploy rebased branches
To keep the history strictly linear so that git bisect works on every commit
items.explanation: The merge history literally names every story: 'Merge PR #1' through 'Merge PR #19' covering HN-01..HN-20.

items.prompt: As a reviewer you notice a missing test for new estimator logic and, separately, a variable name you would have chosen differently. How should you label them?
distractors: Both blocking, so the author fixes everything before the merge
Both are nits, since tests can always follow in a later PR
The naming is blocking for consistency; the missing test is a question
items.explanation: Blocking covers correctness, security, data loss and missing tests for new logic; style and taste are nits.

items.prompt: You finished 4 of a story's 5 acceptance criteria and the fifth needs a HubSpot property that doesn't exist yet. What does the definition of done require?
items.answer: Record the unfinished criterion in the PR or a follow-up issue
distractors: Mark the story done, since the blocker is outside your control
Hold the PR open until someone creates the HubSpot property, then finish the story
Delete the fifth criterion
items.explanation: Done means every criterion is demonstrably met, or what could not be finished is explicitly recorded.

items.prompt: A teammate committed and pushed an API token, then deleted the file in the next commit. What is the first thing to do?
distractors: Rewrite the history with git filter-repo and force-push every branch
Nothing more: deleting the file in the next commit removed the secret
Add the file to .gitignore so the token cannot be committed again
items.explanation: Deleting the file does not remove the secret: it is still in the history of every clone and fork. Until the old value is revoked nothing else matters; untracking, ignoring and optional history rewriting come after.

items.prompt: Why must a credential never be placed in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment variable?
items.answer: They are inlined into the browser bundle at build time
distractors: They are printed to the Amplify build console
They are only available on the server, so client code that reads them would break
They are committed to the repository automatically by the Amplify CLI on every push
items.explanation: Treat NEXT_PUBLIC_ values as if printed on the homepage: configuration, not secrets.

items.prompt: As inherited, the estimator subscribed to onUpdateProject without variables and checked the id in the browser. What was actually wrong with that?
items.answer: Every visitor's browser received every other visitor's project updates
distractors: Nothing beyond wasted bandwidth, since mismatched updates were discarded
Missed own updates
It made the AI enrichment worker process each submitted project twice
items.explanation: Without variables AppSync pushed every project update to every connected client; the client-side id check hid a data leak instead of preventing it. The fix passes filter: { id: { eq: projectId } } and keeps the client check as defence in depth (HN-10).

items.prompt: Why was `@auth(rules: [{ allow: public, provider: identityPool }])` with no operations dangerous on every @model type?
items.answer: No operations listed means all are granted, to anonymous guests
distractors: It forced users to sign in
It blocked subscriptions entirely, so the estimator had to fall back to polling
It made only the read operations public; the write operations were already protected
items.explanation: Identity-pool guest credentials ship in the bundle, so any visitor could call listLeads (PII) or deleteProject. The fix grants only what the app calls, e.g. Project: create, get, listen.

items.prompt: Project now grants anonymous `get` but not `list`. What property does that give the project id?
items.answer: A capability token: whoever knows the id can read the estimate
distractors: None: get and list are equivalent once a client holds guest credentials
A public identifier, safe to list
It is encrypted by AppSync before it ever reaches the visitor's browser
items.explanation: get by id is needed for polling and shareable links, while list is withheld because it would expose every visitor's scope and budget; so no UI may ever enumerate ids.

items.prompt: Why does the estimator POST to '/api/create-hubspot-lead/' with a trailing slash?
items.answer: trailingSlash: true makes the slashless URL redirect, losing the POST body
distractors: Pages Router API routes need it
The trailing slash bypasses the rate limiter for internal same-origin calls
HubSpot's contacts API rejects any request URL that lacks a trailing slash
items.explanation: Internal fetch calls to API routes must include the slash in this repo.

items.prompt: parseTimelineToMonths receives "4-6 months" and then "ASAP". What does it return?
distractors: 4 and 0
6 and 1
5 and NaN
items.explanation: A range is averaged (Math.round((4 + 6) / 2) = 5), and text with no number falls back to a conservative 12 months, because under-estimating a timeline under-estimates cost.

items.front: The two Plasmic rules in HyperNova
items.back: 1) Never edit anything under components/plasmic/: it is regenerated on every design sync. 2) All behaviour goes in the hand-written wrapper (e.g. components/ContactForm.tsx), which passes the generated component overrides, slot content and variants.

items.front: Why the old in-memory rate limiter was wrong on Lambda, and why the new one fails open
items.back: A module-scoped Map starts empty on every cold start, so concurrent instances made the advertised 5-per-15-minutes limit unenforced, and a module-level setInterval kept timers alive. The store is now pluggable (DynamoDB with TTL). If the store is down the request is allowed: abuse prevention must not become an outage that loses real leads.

items.front: What is surprising about this repo's pre-commit hook?
items.back: It runs npm run lint and then `git add -A` if anything is unstaged, so it stages everything in your working tree, including files you deliberately left out of the commit.

items.front: What happens now when the AI analysis never arrives (after 6 polls)?
items.back: The estimator sets aiStatus 'degraded', pushes an estimator_ai_timeout event and shows the summary as a preliminary estimate. Previously it silently showed the local baseline, indistinguishable from a real analysis (HN-06).
